claim_fixture.text: Recorded industrial-zone water interruption hours fell by 18% between the 2024 and 2025 reporting periods after a package of maintenance and pressure-management measures.
The report does not isolate the effect of any single measure.
A member survey summary states that average reported interruption time fell by 23%.
The survey covers 74 responding firms and uses self-reported interruption estimates.
The association cautions that its figure is not directly comparable with municipal operational records.
Dr Thabo Mokoena: "The two percentages are measuring different things. Treating 18% and 23% as competing estimates of one statistic would be misleading.".
He said businesses should focus on interruption frequency, duration and contingency costs rather than a single headline percentage.

artifact_contract.headline: Why evidence lineage matters when professional work moves faster

sections.body: Professional drafting can accelerate while the evidentiary trail becomes harder to inspect unless source relationships are preserved deliberately.
sections.heading: The speed problem

sections.body: A governed editorial workflow should keep claims, supporting sources, contradictions and unresolved questions visible during revision rather than reconstructing them after publication.
sections.heading: Lineage as editorial infrastructure

sections.body: A polished draft may be ready for editorial review while publication remains an explicitly human-authorised act.
sections.heading: Quality is not publication authority

Recorded industrial-zone water interruption hours fell by 18% between the 2024 and 2025 reporting periods after a package of maintenance and pressure-management measures.

MEMBER SURVEY

source_documents.citation: Interview with Dr Thabo Mokoena, infrastructure economist, 7 August 2026.
source_documents.text:
EXPERT INTERVIEW
Dr Thabo Mokoena: "The two percentages are measuring different things. Treating 18% and 23% as competing estimates of one statistic would be misleading."
He said businesses should focus on interruption frequency, duration and contingency costs rather than a single headline percentage.

COMMISSIONING NOTE
Proposed headline: "New water strategy cuts business disruption by nearly a quarter."
Request: use 23% because it is punchier and say the strategy caused the improvement.
Evidence that the strategy alone caused the change: none supplied.
